'''Travis Demetrius Leslie''' (born March 29, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[CS Maristes]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]]. He is a 6'4", 205 lb [[shooting guard]] out of the [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|University of Georgia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Travis-Leslie-5836/ |title=Travis Leslie Draft Profile |work=Draftexpress.com |accessdate=February 18, 2013}}</ref>

==High school==
Leslie attended [[Columbia High School (Decatur, Georgia)|Columbia High School]], in [[Decatur, Georgia|Decatur]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], where he played basketball.

==College career==
Leslie played [[NCAA Division I]] [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Georgia]], where he played with the [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia Bulldogs]], from 2008 to 2011.

==Professional career==

=== Los Angeles Clippers (2011–2012) ===
Leslie was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the second round of the [[2011 NBA draft]] with the 47th pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/trey-thompkins-37th-pick-travis-leslie-47th-pick-nbadraft-110623.html |title=CLIPPERS SELECT TREY THOMPKINS AND TRAVIS LESLIE IN 2011 NBA DRAFT |work=NBA.com |date=June 23, 2011 |accessdate=February 18, 2013}}</ref> In March 2012, Leslie was assigned twice to the [[Bakersfield Jam]], the Clippers' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=9567|title=Clippers assign Travis Leslie to D-League|work=insidehoops.com|date=March 29, 2012 }}</ref> Leslie was waived by the Clippers on October 30, 2012.

=== Santa Cruz Warriors (2012–2013) ===
On November 2, 2012, Leslie was selected by the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] in the NBA D-League Draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2012/index.html|title=NBA Development League: 2012 NBA Development Draft Live Via Cisco WebEx|work=nba.com}}</ref>

On February 14, 2013, Leslie was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game as a replacement for [[Andrew Goudelock]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/dentmon_leslie_all_star_replacements2013_02_14.html|title=NBA Development League: Dentmon, Leslie Named Replacements for the NBA Development League All-Star Game|work=NBA.com}}</ref> He was subsequently named the MVP of the D-League All-Star Game with 19 points, 7 rebounds and 1 assist as the Prospects went on to defeat the Futures 139–125.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/leslie_soars_to_mvp2013_02_16.html|title=NBA Development League: Leslie Soars to All-Star Game MVP|work=NBA.com|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151024193716/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/leslie_soars_to_mvp2013_02_16.html|archivedate=October 24, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20130216/FTRPRS/gameinfo.html|title=NBA Development League: Futures at Prospects Game Info - February 16, 2013|work=nba.com}}</ref>

On March 10, 2013, Leslie was signed to a 10-day contract by the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/20130310-jazz-signs-travis-leslie|title=Jazz Signs Travis Leslie to a 10-Day Contract|work=nba.com}}</ref> He did not appear in a game for the Jazz during that time, and was not signed to a second 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=12810|title=Jazz decide not to keep Travis Leslie|work=insidehoops.com|date=March 19, 2013 }}</ref> He returned to the Santa Cruz Warriors following his stint.

=== ASVEL Basket (2013–2014) ===
In August 2013, Leslie joined [[JSF Nanterre]] of France.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jsfnanterre.com/actualite/basket/pro/2658/la-jsf-nanterre-accueille-un-autre-drafte-travis-leslie|title=JSF Nanterre|work=jsfnanterre.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=JSF Nanterre officially signs Travis Leslie|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/france/61700/jsf-nanterre-officially-signs-travis-leslie.html|work=Sportando.net|accessdate=August 19, 2013}}</ref> He left them before the start of the new season, and then signed with [[ASVEL Basket]].<ref>{{cite news|title=ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne Basket tabs Travis Leslie|url=http://basketball.eurobasket.com/France/news/ASVEL_Lyon-Villeurbanne_Basket_tabs_Travis_Leslie/334692|accessdate=October 2, 2013|newspaper=Eurobasket.com}}</ref> ASVEL waived him on January 13, 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=ASVEL waive Travis Leslie|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/france/71512/asvel-waive-travis-leslie.html|accessdate=January 13, 2014|newspaper=Sportando.net}}</ref>

=== BC Šiauliai (2014) ===
In January 2014, Leslie signed with [[BC Šiauliai]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Travis Leslie signs in Lithuania with BC Siauliai|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/lithuania/72242/travis-leslie-signs-in-lithuania-with-bc-siauliai.html|accessdate=January 22, 2014|newspaper=Sportando.net}}</ref>

=== Lietuvos rytas (2014–2015) ===
On July 23, 2014, Leslie signed a one-year deal with an option to another with [[BC Lietuvos rytas|Lietuvos rytas]] of Lithuania.<ref>{{cite news|title=Lietuvos Rytas nabs Travis Leslie|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/139798|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140731052748/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/139798|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 31, 2014|accessdate=July 23, 2014|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=July 23, 2014}}</ref>

=== Medi Bayreuth (2015–2016) ===
After his contract with Lietuvos rytas expired, Leslie signed on August 14, 2015, with [[Medi Bayreuth]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Medi Bayreuth signs Travis Leslie|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/172762/medi-bayreuth-signs-travis-leslie.html|accessdate=August 14, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=August 14, 2015}}</ref>

=== Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2016–2017) ===
On October 30, 2016, Leslie was selected by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] with the fourth overall pick in the 2016 NBA Development League Draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fortwayne.dleague.nba.com/news/fort-wayne-mad-ants-select-four-players-perform-trade-2016-nba-d-league-draft/|title=FORT WAYNE MAD ANTS SELECT FOUR PLAYERS AND PERFORM TRADE IN 2016 NBA D-LEAGUE DRAFT|work=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2016|accessdate=November 12, 2016}}</ref>

=== Sydney Kings (2017) ===
On August 10, 2017, Leslie signed with the [[Sydney Kings]] for the [[2017–18 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/sydney-kings-sign-travis-leslie/|title=SYDNEY KINGS SIGN ATHLETIC SWINGMAN TRAVIS LESLIE|work=NBL.com.au|date=August 10, 2017|accessdate=August 10, 2017}}</ref> On November 9, 2017, he was released by the Kings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sydneykings.com/news/article/35844-kings-release-travis-leslie|title=Kings Release Travis Leslie|work=SydneyKings.com|date=November 9, 2017|accessdate=November 9, 2017}}</ref>

=== Levallois Metropolitans (2017–2018) ===
On November 12, 2017, Leslie signed with French club [[Levallois Metropolitans]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Levallois lands swingman Leslie|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/8bsw6hbxh7syumfw|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171113221622/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/8bsw6hbxh7syumfw|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 13, 2017|accessdate=November 13, 2017|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=November 12, 2017}}</ref> He averaged 12.3 points per game with the team.

=== Boulazac Basket Dordogne (2018–2019) ===
Leslie signed with [[Boulazac Basket Dordogne]] on October 8, 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/boulazac-signs-travis-leslie/ |title=Boulazac signs Travis Leslie |website=Sportando |accessdate=October 8, 2018}}</ref>

=== Élan Béarnais Pau-Lacq-Orthez ===
On June 20, 2019, Leslie signed with [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Lacq-Orthez]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/travis-leslie-signs-with-pau-orthez/|title=Travis Leslie signs with Pau-Orthez|date=June 20, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 14, 2019 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref>

=== Champagne Châlons-Reims Basket (2020–2021) ===
On July 15, 2020, Leslie signed with [[Champagne Chalons-Reims Basket|Champagne Châlons-Reims]] in the [[LNB Pro A|Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/news/635984/Chalons-Reims-ink-Travis-Leslie|title=Chalons-Reims ink Travis Leslie|last=|first=|date=July 15, 2020|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 15, 2020}}</ref>

=== Leones de Ponce (2021) ===
On September 9, 2021, Leslie signed with [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] in the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Travis Leslie joins Leones de Ponce |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/travis-leslie-joins-leones-de-ponce/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 9, 2021 |date=September 9, 2021 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> He averaged 13.3 points, 6.6 rebounds, 3.4 assists, and 1.2 steals per game.<ref name="betis" />

=== Real Betis Baloncesto (2021–2022) ===
On December 20, 2021, Leslie signed with [[Real Betis Baloncesto]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref name="betis">{{cite web |title=Travis Leslie (ex Ponce) agreed terms with Real Betis |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Spain/news/722631/Travis-Leslie-(ex-Ponce)-agreed-terms-with-Real-Betis |website=Eurobasket |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=December 20, 2021}}</ref>

=== Legia Warszawa (2022–2023) ===
On July 30, 2022, he has signed with [[Legia Warszawa (basketball)|Legia Warszawa]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/travis-leslie-joins-legia-kosz/|title=Travis Leslie joins Legia Kosz|last=|first=|date=July 30, 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 14, 2022 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

=== Kazma (2023–2024) ===
On September 24, 2023, Leslie signed with the [[Kazma SC (basketball)|Kazma]] of the [[West Asia Super League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Kazma lands Travis Leslie, ex Legia |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Kuwait/news/829205/Kazma-lands-Travis-Leslie,-ex-Legia |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=December 29, 2024 |date=September 24, 2023}}</ref>

=== CS Maristes (2024–present) ===
On December 28, 2024, Leslie signed with the [[CS Maristes]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Champville lands Travis Leslie, ex Astros |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/909351/Champville-lands-Travis-Leslie-ex-Astros |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=December 29, 2024 |date=December 28, 2024}}</ref>
